title: Auditable write-lease & proof-of-origin for cross-region analytics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Console emits high-cardinality usage events (token counts, route metadata, per-token latencies) that are consumed by the analytics pipeline. Customers in regulated regions require provable locality and an auditable chain-of-custody for writes. Current replication creates multiple writable mirrors and relies on eventual reconciliation which makes it hard to prove origin or detect silent duplication/replay across regions.

Goal: Implement a light-weight auditable write-lease and proof-of-origin mechanism that: (1) guarantees a single authoritative write owner for a tenant-day shard, (2) attaches a tamper-evident proof to each batch so downstream systems can verify origin and detect replays, and (3) integrates with existing replication/fanout so we can enforce residency policies without increasing end-to-end latency significantly.

Design sketch:
- Lease model: a short-lived (1h) signed write-lease per (tenant, partition, region) issued by the control plane. Leases carry a monotonic sequence base and an expiry. Only the holder can submit incrementing batch sequence ranges.
- Proof-of-origin: each batch is signed using an HMAC key tied to the lease. The signature covers tenant id, sequence range, region tag, and a root hash over event IDs. The control plane records the lease issuance event to an append-only ledger (kafka topic with compacted retention + signed checkpoint).
- Replay protection: downstream consumers validate sequence monotonicity and lease ID; duplicates or out-of-order batches are flagged and routed to a quarantine topic for manual/reconcile flow.
- Local ephemeral ledger: to avoid cross-region round-trips, the local proxy persists batch metadata to a local write-ahead ledger (rocksdb) and forwards signed batches asynchronously to replication topics. The ledger is pruned on lease expiry+consensus checkpoint.
- Reconciliation service: periodic background reconciliation reads compacted ledger snapshots across regions to verify a consistent lineage; discrepancies generate alerts and attach forensic data for support.
- Backcompat: for tenants not enrolled in residency controls, the system will operate in pass-through mode (no leases), preserving current behaviour. Enrollment is opt-in per tenant.

Trade-offs & considerations:
- Latency: adding signing/ledger writes can add ~2-6ms p99; mitigations: HMAC via shared key and local WAL + async push reduces added latency for the fast path.
- Key management: requires KMS integration for lease HMAC keys. We will rotate per-lease keys using envelope encryption (KMS-wrapped symmetric key).
- Complexity: introduces more moving parts in the console backend; to limit blast radius we scope initial rollout to console events only (no inferred telemetry) and a single region pair for testing.

Success criteria:
- Every admitted batch in enrolled tenants carries a valid lease ID and signature.
- Quarantine rate for enrolled tenants < 0.05% after 2 weeks of run-in.
- Reconciliation job can assert lineage for > 99.9% of batches in the last 7 days.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Implementation behind feature flag in dev cluster, unit+integration tests.
2) Canary: enroll 2 internal tenants, enable in console region A->B. Monitor p99 latency, doorbell alerts.
3) Gradual enroll: add automation for opt-in via tenant metadata; expand to selected EU customers.
4) Hardening: KMS key rotation automation, audit dashboards, runbook for quarantine/resolution.

Monitoring & observability:
- Metrics: lease_issue_rate, lease_sign_latency_ms{p50,p90,p99}, batch_signature_failures, quarantine_rate, reconciliation_failures.
- Traces: end-to-end trace for batch from ingress -> ledger write -> replication -> consumer ack.
- Dashboards: per-tenant lineage health and recent quarantine examples.

Security/compliance notes: storing lease metadata in a compacted kafka topic makes it auditable; we will enable message signing and encrypt-at-rest for those topics. Security review is required before canary enrollment.
acceptance_criteria: Signed lease issued and recorded for each enrolled tenant partition within 1 hour windows
Ingress path attaches lease HMAC to every batch and consumer validates signature in test harness
Reconciliation job produces lineage report and reconciles > 99.9% of recent batches
Feature flag allows per-tenant opt-in and false positives can be quarantined without data loss

Operational burden of quarantined batches and manual reconciliation
